name: io.github.keithdealwis-ui/the-source
title: The Source
description: Discover 25,000+ projects, find open-source alternatives, compare health and track surging momentum.

tools.name: source_dataset_info
tools.description: Which snapshot of The Source is being served: dataset_version, data_as_of, when repositories were last checked (and whether that is stale), record counts, upstream sources, licence and attribution. Answers are compact by default: blocks named in include (signals, corpus and meta state, notes, explanations, retrieval, evidence, topics, links) are left out or cut to their status and freshness fields, and the answer's response.left_out lists them; tier, recommended flags, licence_disclosure, live_checked_at / observed_as_of, attribution and any *_reason, capped or suppressed field are always kept. Pass detail "full" for every block, or include to bring named blocks back.

detail.description: compact (default): leave out state, explanatory and evidence blocks; full: every block

include.description: compact only: blocks to keep, e.g. ['signals', 'evidence']

'saas' may be a saas_id, a name, an alias, a domain or a URL. For supported products this is exactly the published api/v1 page (with detail full; compact cuts each row's evidence block to its dates). tools.name: source_search
tools.description: Search The Source's SaaS catalogue and every open-source project it knows (about 9,400: the canonical layer plus the discovery corpus) by words: names, aliases, categories, products replaced, host descriptions and topics. Every project carries a tier (recommended, scored, discovery); filter by tier, licence, maintenance status and Project Health (or quick Health). Discovery projects are not fully scored and never recommendations; they carry labelled quick Health and quick Fit (KEI-921). Answers are compact by default: blocks named in include (signals, corpus and meta state, notes, explanations, retrieval, evidence, topics, links) are left out or cut to their status and freshness fields, and the answer's response.left_out lists them; tier, recommended flags, licence_disclosure, live_checked_at / observed_as_of, attribution and any *_reason, capped or suppressed field are always kept. Pass detail "full" for every block, or include to bring named blocks back.

include.description: compact only: blocks to keep, e.g. ['signals', 'evidence']

min_quick_health.description: projects: discovery rows by quick Health; canonical rows by their full Project Health (quick scores are never recommendations)

mode.description: lexical (default, BM25) or hybrid (BM25 + KEI-844 semantic + graph, with score components per result)

query.description: words to look for, e.g. 'password manager'

supported_only.description: SaaS results: only products with a page

tier.description: projects only: recommended, scored or discovery (default any)

tools.name: source_compare_projects
tools.description: Side by side for 2-5 projects: licence, stars, maintenance, Project Health, Replacement Fit for every SaaS product they replace (head to head where they share one), Repository Momentum and Community Momentum, with the uncertainty in each. The four measures are kept separate. Discovery-tier projects can be compared too; they have no Project Health or Replacement Fit and say so. tools.name: source_recommend
tools.description: Recommended open-source projects for a need in words and/or a SaaS product to replace, filtered exactly by hard constraints (licence or licence family, self-hostable, maintenance, minimum Replacement Fit or Project Health, star range, days since activity, 7-day repository momentum). Says which products the need matched and how (lexical, KEI-844 semantic, graph), what each constraint excluded, and which requirements the data cannot judge.
